exposure: Herbal tea of M. stenopetala and M. spicata leaves formulation (559.36, 1118.72, and 2237.44 mg/kg)
outcome: Maternal systemic toxicity (body weight, serum biochemistry, organ weight, macro-pathology)
Reproductive toxicity (number of corpora lutea, implantations, resorptions, pre/postimplantation losses, number of fetuses (live/dead), fetal body weights, fetal length, fetal sex ratio)
cohort: 32 pregnant Wistar rats were randomly distributed into four groups of 8.
finding: The herbal tea of M. stenopetala and M. spicata leaves blend was relatively safe/low toxic to pregnant rats and developing fetuses, with a no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) for maternal toxicity, fetotoxicity, and teratogenicity estimated to be > 2237.44 mg/kg/day.
gest_age: Evaluation was performed on gestation day 20.
